ws.e: perform sacrifice — iṣṭa (sacrifice, from √yaj) + kurvanti (they do); ritual is aligned with cosmic rhythms

gr: māsaḥ vai prajāpatiḥ — 'the month is Prajāpati': having identified the year with Prajāpati, now the month is also Prajāpati — the same creative principle operates at every temporal scale. kṛṣṇa-pakṣaḥ = rayiḥ; śuklaḥ = prāṇaḥ — the Prāṇa-Rayi framework is applied to the lunar cycle: waning moon = matter (darkness, diminishing), waxing moon = life-force (light, growing). śukle iṣṭaṁ kurvanti — 'they perform sacrifice in the bright half': the wise align their rituals with the Prāṇa-principle (light, growth). This is a practical application of the cosmological teaching.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: prashna_upanishad_1.12 — The Prāṇa-Rayi framework is here applied to the month: bright fortnight = Prāṇa, dark fortnight = Rayi. The preference for performing rituals in the śukla-pakṣa is a general Vedic principle — auspicious rites are typically performed during the waxing moon. The Bhagavad Gītā (8.24-25) correlates these with the devayāna and pitṛyāṇa: 'agniḥ jyotiḥ ahaḥ śuklaḥ ... tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma' (bright fortnight → Brahman, no return) vs. 'dhūmaḥ rātriḥ kṛṣṇaḥ ... prāpya nivartante' (dark fortnight → return).

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — शुक्लपक्ष = प्रकाश = ज्ञान; कृष्णपक्ष = अन्धकार = अज्ञान। ज्ञानी प्रकाश-काल (शुक्ल) में कर्म करते हैं — यह प्रतीकात्मक भी है: ज्ञान-प्रधान जीवन = शुक्ल; अज्ञान-प्रधान = कृष्ण।
advaita.en: Shankara says bright half = light = knowledge; dark half = darkness = ignorance. The wise perform actions during the light period (śukla) — this is also symbolic: a knowledge-oriented life = bright; an ignorance-oriented life = dark.
advaita.ins: The universe teaches through its rhythms. The moon waxes: that is Prāṇa growing. The moon wanes: that is Rayi reclaiming. Align your actions with the light — work when consciousness is growing.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — शुक्लपक्ष = भगवान् की प्रकाश-शक्ति; कृष्णपक्ष = भगवान् की संहारक शक्ति। ऋषि शुक्ल-काल में उपासना करते हैं — प्रकाश की दिशा में, भगवान् की ओर।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says the bright half = the Lord's power of light; the dark half = the Lord's power of dissolution. The sages worship in the bright period — in the direction of light, toward the Lord.
vishisht.ins: Even time has a direction. The wise choose the half that grows toward fullness. Let your life face the light.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — शुक्ल/कृष्ण = चेतना के विकास (ascending) और अवरोह (descending) चरण। ऋषि विकास-चरण (ascending phase) में आध्यात्मिक कार्य करते हैं — जब चेतना प्राकृतिक रूप से ऊर्ध्वगामी होती है।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo reads bright/dark as ascending and descending phases of consciousness. Sages perform spiritual work in the ascending phase — when consciousness is naturally upward-moving.
aurobindo.ins: There are tides in consciousness, as in the ocean. The wise swim with the rising tide. Align your deepest work with the moments when the light is naturally growing.

dp.q: 🔍 Why does the Prashna map Prāṇa-Rayi onto everything?
dp.a: The Prashna Upanishad systematically applies its Prāṇa-Rayi framework to every level of reality: Cosmic: sun = Prāṇa, moon = Rayi. Annual: uttarāyaṇa = Prāṇa, dakṣiṇāyana = Rayi. Monthly: bright fortnight = Prāṇa, dark fortnight = Rayi. Daily (in the next verse): day = Prāṇa, night = Rayi. This pervasive application serves a philosophical purpose: the same duality operates at every scale. The universe is fractal — the pattern that governs the cosmos (sun-moon) governs the year (north-south), the month (bright-dark), the day (day-night), and even the individual body (prāṇa-apāna). This means: if you understand the Prāṇa-Rayi duality at ANY level, you understand it at ALL levels. The microcosm reflects the macrocosm. And it means: spiritual practice can be aligned with cosmic rhythms. By choosing the Prāṇa-dominant phase (day over night, bright half over dark, uttarāyaṇa over dakṣiṇāyana), the seeker harnesses the natural momentum of the cosmos. This is not superstition but conscious alignment — working with the grain of reality rather than against it.

dp.q: 🔍 What is the lunar calendar and why does it matter spiritually?
dp.a: The Vedic calendar is primarily lunar — months are reckoned by the phases of the moon, not the sun. Each month consists of two pakṣas (fortnights): the śukla-pakṣa (bright half, new moon to full moon, 15 days of waxing) and the kṛṣṇa-pakṣa (dark half, full moon to new moon, 15 days of waning). The moon's phases are not merely astronomical observations — they are indices of cosmic energy. The waxing moon represents growth, increase, light, consciousness, ascent — the Prāṇa principle. The waning moon represents decrease, dissolution, darkness, matter, descent — the Rayi principle. In Vedic ritual practice, this translates directly into timing: auspicious rites (marriages, initiations, new beginnings) are generally performed during the śukla-pakṣa. Rites for the ancestors (śrāddha, pitṛ-tarpaṇa) are typically performed during the kṛṣṇa-pakṣa — because the ancestors belong to the pitṛyāṇa (the Rayi-path). This cosmic alignment is not arbitrary superstition — it reflects the Upanishadic insight that individual action is most effective when synchronised with cosmic rhythms.

sk: अहोरात्रो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्याहरेव प्राणो रात्रिरेव रयिः प्राणं वा एते प्रस्कन्दन्ति ये दिवा रत्या संयुज्यन्ते ब्रह्मचर्यमेव तद्यद्रात्रौ रत्या संयुज्यन्ते ||
ro: ahoratraḥ · vai · prajāpatiḥ · tasya · ahaḥ · eva · prāṇaḥ · rātriḥ · eva · rayiḥ · prāṇaṁ · vā · ete · praskandanti · ye · divā · ratyā · saṁyujyante · brahmacaryam · eva · tat · yat · rātrau · ratyā · saṁyujyante ||
hi: अहोरात्र (दिन-रात) ही प्रजापति है; उसका दिन प्राण है, रात्रि रयि है। जो दिन में रति (मैथुन / यौन-संगम) करते हैं, वे प्राण को स्कन्दित (नष्ट / बिखेर) करते हैं। रात्रि में रति करना — वही ब्रह्मचर्य (संयम) के तुल्य है।
en: The day-and-night is Prajāpati; its daytime is Prāṇa, its nighttime is Rayi. Those who unite in sexual pleasure during the day dissipate their Prāṇa. To unite at night — that alone is (consonant with) brahmacarya.

ws.e: day-and-night — the daily cycle, now identified with Prajāpati, continuing the fractal application

ws.h: प्रस्कन्दित करते हैं / बिखेरते हैं / नष्ट करते हैं
ws.e: dissipate / waste — pra + √skand (to leap/spill); vital energy is 'scattered' or 'spilled' when expended during the Prāṇa-phase (daytime)
with sexual pleasure — rati (love-making, from √ram, to delight); conjugal union

ws.h: संयुक्त होते हैं / मैथुन करते हैं
ws.e: unite — sam + √yuj (to yoke together); sexual union
that alone is (equivalent to) brahmacarya — the surprising claim: conjugal union at the proper time (night = Rayi-phase) is not a violation of brahmacarya but consonant with it

gr: ahoratraḥ vai prajāpatiḥ — 'the day-and-night is Prajāpati': the Prāṇa-Rayi framework now reaches the daily cycle. Day = Prāṇa (light, activity, consciousness); night = Rayi (darkness, rest, matter). prāṇaṁ praskandanti — 'they dissipate Prāṇa': sexual activity during the daytime (the Prāṇa-phase) wastes vital energy because it is out of alignment with the cosmic rhythm. brahmacaryam eva tat yat rātrau ratyā saṁyujyante — 'union at night IS brahmacarya': this is a remarkable and pragmatic teaching. The Upanishad does NOT demand total celibacy for householders — it asks for alignment with cosmic rhythms. Conjugal union at night (the Rayi-phase, when procreative energy is naturally active) is compatible with the spirit of brahmacarya.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: prashna_upanishad_1.13 — This verse is notable for its pragmatic, non-ascetic approach to sexuality. Unlike later renunciant traditions that demand absolute celibacy, the Prashna frames sexual discipline in terms of cosmic alignment: the issue is not the act itself but its timing. Day = Prāṇa (vital energy is active and should be conserved); night = Rayi (procreative/material energy is naturally dominant). This teaching is directed at gṛhasthas (householders), not sannyāsins. The concept of 'prāṇa-skandana' (dissipation of vital energy) anticipates later Yoga and Āyurveda teachings about ojas (vital essence) conservation.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — यह गृहस्थ-धर्म का निर्देश है, संन्यास का नहीं। दिन = प्राण-काल (ऊर्जा-संचय); रात = रयि-काल (प्रजनन)। दिन में मैथुन = प्राण-हानि; रात में = प्राकृतिक ताल (natural rhythm) के अनुकूल — इसलिए 'ब्रह्मचर्य' कहा।
advaita.en: Shankara says this is instruction for householders, not renunciants. Day = Prāṇa-period (energy conservation); night = Rayi-period (procreation). Daytime union = Prāṇa-loss; nighttime = in harmony with natural rhythm — hence called 'brahmacarya.'
advaita.ins: The Upanishad does not demand the impossible. For the householder, it asks not abstinence but alignment. Work with the rhythm of nature, not against it.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — गृहस्थ-धर्म में ऋतु-काल (proper time) में मैथुन कर्तव्य है — यह 'ब्रह्मचर्य' के विरुद्ध नहीं। 'प्राण-स्कन्दन' — अनुचित काल में मैथुन करने से ऊर्जा क्षय और आध्यात्मिक हानि होती है।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says in householder life, conjugal union at the proper time (ṛtu-kāla) is a duty — not opposed to brahmacarya. 'Prāṇa-skandana' — union at improper times causes energy depletion and spiritual harm.
vishisht.ins: Dharma does not fight nature — it channels it. The householder's brahmacarya is not abstinence but discipline: the right thing, at the right time, in the right way.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'प्राण-स्कन्दन' = vital energy (ओजस्) का अपव्यय। दिन में चेतना ऊर्ध्वगामी (ascending) होती है — उस समय यौन-ऊर्जा को अधोगामी (descending) करना हानिकारक है। रात में ऊर्जा स्वाभाविक रूप से अवरोही है।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo reads 'prāṇa-skandana' as the waste of vital energy (ojas). During the day, consciousness is naturally ascending — diverting sexual energy downward then is harmful. At night, energy is naturally descending.
aurobindo.ins: The body has its own wisdom. During the day it wants to rise, to act, to create; at night it wants to descend, to rest, to regenerate. Work with these tides, not against them.

dp.q: 🔍 Does the Upanishad allow sexual activity for seekers?
dp.a: This verse offers one of the most pragmatic and psychologically realistic teachings in the Upanishads regarding sexuality. The answer is nuanced: For householders (gṛhasthas): yes, with conditions. The Upanishad does not demand absolute celibacy for householders. Instead, it prescribes cosmic alignment: conjugal union at night (the Rayi-phase) is declared compatible with brahmacarya. The key word is 'brahmacaryam eva tat' — 'THAT IS brahmacarya.' This is a remarkable statement: the Upanishad is redefining brahmacarya not as total abstinence but as disciplined alignment with cosmic rhythms. The prohibition is against daytime union, which 'dissipates Prāṇa' (prāṇaṁ praskandanti). The reasoning: during the day, vital energy (prāṇa) is naturally ascending and active — it should be directed toward work, worship, and knowledge. Diverting it toward sexual activity during this phase 'spills' the energy that should be conserved. At night, the body is in its Rayi-phase (rest, materiality, regeneration) — procreative activity aligns with this natural rhythm. For renunciants (sannyāsins): the verse is addressed to ṛṣis who are 'prajā-kāma' (desiring offspring) — i.e., householders. Complete celibacy remains the standard for renunciants. The Upanishad's teaching is context-sensitive, not one-size-fits-all.

dp.q: 🔍 What is 'prāṇa-skandana' (dissipation of vital energy)?
dp.a: Prāṇa-skandana (pra + √skand, 'to spill/leap/scatter') means the dissipation or wasting of vital energy. The concept anticipates later Yoga and Āyurveda teachings about ojas (vital essence). In the Āyurvedic model, ojas is the finest product of digestion — the concentrated essence of all the body's seven dhātus (tissues). Sexual activity expends ojas. When ojas is depleted, the body becomes vulnerable to disease, aging, and mental dullness. When ojas is conserved, the body glows with health, the mind is clear, and the spirit is strong. The Yoga tradition similarly teaches that ūrdhva-retas (upward flow of sexual energy) is essential for higher spiritual experiences. The kuṇḍalinī tradition describes sexual energy as the same force that, when redirected upward through the suṣumnā nāḍī, activates the higher chakras and leads to samādhi. The Prashna's teaching is the earliest version of this insight: vital energy (Prāṇa) should not be 'scattered' (praskandita) during the wrong phase of the cosmic cycle. The emphasis is not on guilt or sin but on energy management — a remarkably modern, pragmatic approach to a topic often shrouded in moralism.

sk: अन्नं वै प्रजापतिस्ततो ह वै तद्रेतस्तस्मादिमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते ||
ro: annaṁ · vai · prajāpatiḥ · tataḥ · ha · vai · tat · retaḥ · tasmāt · imāḥ · prajāḥ · prajāyante ||
hi: अन्न (भोजन) ही प्रजापति है; उसी से रेतस् (वीर्य / बीज) उत्पन्न होता है; उसी से ये प्रजाएँ (जीव) उत्पन्न होती हैं।
en: Food (anna) indeed is Prajāpati; from that comes seed (retas); from that these creatures are born.

ws.e: food — from √ad (to eat); food is the material basis of all life; here identified with Prajāpati because it is the substance from which bodies and progeny arise
seed / semen — retas (from √rī, to flow); the generative substance; food transforms into bodily tissues and ultimately into the seed of reproduction

ws.h: उत्पन्न होती हैं / जन्म लेती हैं
ws.e: are born — pra + √jan; the cycle: food → seed → creatures

gr: annaṁ vai prajāpatiḥ — 'food is Prajāpati': the identification shifts from cosmic (sun, moon, year) to material — food is the creative principle at the physical level. tataḥ retaḥ — 'from that comes seed': this is the Āyurvedic chain in embryo: food → bodily tissues (dhātus) → retas (seed/semen). The body transforms food into the generative substance. tasmāt imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante — 'from that these creatures are born': the complete cycle — food becomes seed, seed becomes creatures, creatures eat food, food becomes seed again. This is the Rayi-principle at its most concrete: matter circulating through forms.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: prashna_upanishad_1.14 — The identification anna = Prajāpati connects to the Taittirīya Upanishad's celebrated declaration (3.2): 'annaṁ brahmeti vyajānāt / annād dhi eva khalv imāni bhūtāni jāyante' — 'He understood: food is Brahman. From food indeed all these beings are born.' The anna-retas-prajā chain (food → seed → offspring) is the biological version of the Prāṇa-Rayi cosmology: food (Rayi/matter) is the material substrate from which life (Prāṇa) propagates. This also echoes the Chāndogya (6.2.1-4): Uddalaka's teaching that from food comes retas, from retas comes beings.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — अन्न = रयि (matter) का सर्वाधिक मूर्त (tangible) रूप। अन्न → रेतस् → प्रजा — यह भौतिक सृष्टि-चक्र है। परम सत्य में अन्न = ब्रह्म (तैत्तिरीय 3.2)।
advaita.en: Shankara says food = the most tangible form of Rayi (matter). Food → seed → progeny — this is the physical creation-cycle. In ultimate truth, food = Brahman (Taittirīya 3.2).
advaita.ins: The profoundest truth hides in the most ordinary thing. Food — the meal on your plate — is Prajāpati, the creator. Everything you eat becomes your body, your energy, your children. Never eat without reverence.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — अन्न = भगवान् का पोषक रूप; भगवान् ही अन्न-रूप से सब प्राणियों का भरण-पोषण करते हैं। 'अन्न से रेतस्, रेतस् से प्रजा' — यह भगवान् की सृजन-प्रक्रिया है।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says food = the Lord's nourishing form; the Lord sustains all beings in the form of food. 'From food comes seed, from seed come creatures' — this is the Lord's creative process.
vishisht.ins: When you eat, you receive the Lord. When you nourish your body, the Lord is nourishing you. The cycle of food, seed, and birth is His hands at work in matter.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — अन्न = पदार्थ (matter) जो चेतना (consciousness) का वाहन (vehicle) बनता है। अन्न → रेतस् → प्रजा = चेतना का भौतिक माध्यम से प्रसार (propagation through material medium)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo reads food as matter that becomes the vehicle of consciousness. Food → seed → progeny = consciousness propagating through the material medium.
aurobindo.ins: Even consciousness needs a body. And every body begins as food — digested, transformed, concentrated into seed, and then exploding into new life. The material world is not opposed to the spiritual — it is its vehicle.

dp.q: 🔍 Why is food identified with Prajāpati?
dp.a: The identification anna = Prajāpati (food = the creator) is one of the boldest claims in Upanishadic philosophy. It means: the creator-principle operates through food. This is not metaphor — it is literal. Food is the material substrate of all life. Every living body is made of food. Every cell is built from digested nutrients. Every generation is produced by bodies that were themselves built from food. The chain is: earth → plants (through rain and sunlight) → food → body → seed → offspring → food again. The Taittirīya Upanishad develops this insight into its most famous teaching: 'annaṁ brahmeti vyajānāt' — Bhrigu realised: 'Food is Brahman' (3.2). 'annād dhi eva khalv imāni bhūtāni jāyante / annena jātāni jīvanti / annaṁ prayanty abhisaṁviśanti' — 'From food all beings are born; by food they live; into food they pass at death' (2.2). The philosophical force: the most ordinary, humble substance — the food on your plate — is the creative power of the universe in its most concrete form. This teaching prevents any easy separation of 'spiritual' from 'material.' If food is Prajāpati, then eating is a sacred act, farming is a sacred occupation, and the body (made of food) is a sacred vessel.

dp.q: 🔍 What is the food → seed → offspring chain?
dp.a: The chain anna → retas → prajā (food → seed → offspring) describes the biological mechanism of creation at the physical level. In Āyurvedic physiology, this chain is elaborated as the dhātu-transformation sequence: food (anna) is digested and progressively refined through seven tissue-layers (sapta-dhātu): rasa (chyle) → rakta (blood) → māṁsa (muscle) → meda (fat) → asthi (bone) → majjā (marrow) → śukra/retas (reproductive tissue/seed). Each dhātu feeds the next; the finest product of the entire chain is the generative seed. From seed comes offspring (prajā), and the cycle continues. This model implies that reproductive capacity is the culmination of the entire digestive process — and therefore depends on the quality and quantity of food consumed. It also implies that food quality directly affects offspring quality — a principle embedded in Āyurvedic prenatal care (garbha-saṁskāra). The Upanishad's insight, expressed in one compact verse, anticipates millennia of Indian medical and philosophical thought about the relationship between nutrition, vitality, and procreation.

sk: तद्ये ह वै तत्प्रजापतिव्रतं चरन्ति ते मिथुनमुत्पादयन्ते | तेषामेवैष ब्रह्मलोको येषां तपो ब्रह्मचर्यं येषु सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् ||
ro: tat · ye · ha · vai · tat · prājāpati-vrataṁ · caranti · te · mithunaṁ · utpādayante | teṣām · eva · eṣaḥ · brahma-lokaḥ · yeṣāṁ · tapaḥ · brahmacaryaṁ · yeṣu · satyaṁ · pratiṣṭhitam ||
hi: जो प्रजापतिव्रत (प्रजापति का व्रत — गृहस्थ-धर्म) का पालन करते हैं, वे मिथुन (सन्तान-युगल) उत्पन्न करते हैं। जिनमें तप, ब्रह्मचर्य और सत्य प्रतिष्ठित (स्थापित) हैं — उन्हीं का यह ब्रह्मलोक है।
en: Those who observe the Prajāpati-vow (the householder's discipline) produce offspring. For those in whom austerity, celibacy, and truth are established — for them alone is this world of Brahman.

ws.e: the vow of Prajāpati — the disciplined householder life: producing offspring according to cosmic law (proper time, purity, alignment with Prāṇa-Rayi rhythms)
they produce a pair / offspring — continuing the cosmic process of creation through disciplined procreation
truth is established — satya (truth) + pratiṣṭhita (firmly established); truth must be the foundation, not merely an aspiration

gr: prājāpati-vratam — 'the Prajāpati-vow': the disciplined householder life — producing offspring not for pleasure but as a cosmic duty, in alignment with the Prāṇa-Rayi rhythms taught in this question. te mithunaṁ utpādayante — 'they produce a pair': continuing Prajāpati's original act (mantra 4) — 'these two will make manifold creatures for me.' The householder participates in the cosmic creative process. teṣām eva eṣaḥ brahma-lokaḥ — 'for them alone is the Brahma-world': but this reward is conditional — not on having children but on having tapas, brahmacarya, and satya as foundations. Children without virtue earn no Brahma-world.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: prashna_upanishad_1.15 — This verse bridges the householder path (prājāpati-vrata) and the liberation path (brahma-loka). The three qualifications — tapas, brahmacarya, satya — echo mantra 2's prerequisites (tapas, brahmacarya, śraddhā), with 'satya' (truth) replacing 'śraddhā' (faith). The Muṇḍaka (3.1.5) has a parallel: 'satyena labhyas tapasā hy eṣa ātmā' — 'This Self is attained by truth and by tapas.' The Chāndogya (8.3.5) similarly: 'satyam eva jayati nānṛtam' — 'Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood' (later adopted as India's national motto: Satyameva Jayate).

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'प्रजापतिव्रत' = गृहस्थ-धर्म (regulated householder life)। सन्तान-उत्पत्ति स्वयं मोक्ष का कारण नहीं — केवल तप, ब्रह्मचर्य और सत्य से युक्त होने पर ही 'ब्रह्मलोक' की प्राप्ति होती है।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'prājāpati-vrata' = the regulated householder life. Offspring-production itself is not the cause of mokṣa — only when combined with tapas, brahmacarya, and satya does one attain 'brahma-loka.'
advaita.ins: Having children is not enough. Having children while living in truth, discipline, and purity — that is the Prajāpati-vow. The householder's path is not lesser than the renunciant's — but it has its own fierce discipline.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — प्रजापतिव्रत = भगवान् की सेवा में गृहस्थ-जीवन। 'तप, ब्रह्मचर्य, सत्य' — ये भक्ति के तीन स्तम्भ हैं। 'ब्रह्मलोक' — भगवान् का धाम, जो केवल सत्यनिष्ठ भक्तों को प्राप्त होता है।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says the Prajāpati-vow = householder life in service of the Lord. Tapas, brahmacarya, satya — three pillars of devotion. 'Brahma-loka' = the Lord's abode, attained only by truth-devoted bhaktas.
vishisht.ins: Three pillars hold up the householder's temple: austerity (the walls), continence (the roof), and truth (the foundation). Without truth, the other two cannot stand.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'प्रजापतिव्रत' = सचेतन सृजन — केवल शारीरिक नहीं, अपितु चेतना के स्तर पर भी। 'सत्य प्रतिष्ठितम्' — जिसका जीवन सत्य पर आधारित है, वही ब्रह्म-चेतना का अधिकारी है।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo reads the Prajāpati-vow as conscious creation — not just physical but at the level of consciousness. 'Satya pratiṣṭhitam' — one whose life is founded on truth is fit for Brahman-consciousness.
aurobindo.ins: The householder creates not just children but a field of truth. The house where tapas, brahmacarya, and satya live is already a brahma-loka — a world of Brahman, here on earth.

dp.q: 🔍 What is the 'Prajāpati-vow' (prājāpati-vrata)?
dp.a: The prājāpati-vrata is the disciplined householder's life — the life of one who participates in Prajāpati's creative act through procreation while maintaining spiritual discipline. It is the gṛhastha-dharma (householder's duty) elevated to a cosmic vow. The vow includes: (1) Procreation as duty: producing offspring is not merely personal — it is participation in the cosmic creative process. Prajāpati desired offspring (prajā-kāma, mantra 4); the householder continues this work. (2) Cosmic alignment: conjugal life follows the rhythms of Prāṇa-Rayi (night, not day; proper season; with purity). (3) Three foundations: tapas (austerity — the householder's life is not luxurious), brahmacarya (continence — sexual activity is disciplined, not indiscriminate), satya (truth — the household is founded on honesty, integrity, and authenticity). The remarkable implication: the householder's path can lead to Brahma-loka — the same destination as the renunciant's. This is a powerful validation of the gṛhastha-āśrama in a tradition that often privileges renunciation.

dp.q: 🔍 What is the role of 'satya' (truth) in liberation?
dp.a: The verse lists satya (truth) as the third and culminating foundation — 'yeṣu satyaṁ pratiṣṭhitam' ('in whom truth is established'). Truth occupies a unique position in Upanishadic ethics: it is not merely one virtue among many but the structural foundation of reality itself. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upanishad (5.5.1) declares: 'satyam ity etat / tad yat sat tyad ity etat / sat itaro ayat iti tat satyam' — 'Truth — that which is real (sat) and vital (tya) — that is truth.' The Muṇḍaka (3.1.5) makes it a prerequisite for Self-knowledge: 'satyena labhyas tapasā hy eṣa ātmā' — 'This Self is attained by truth and by tapas.' The Chāndogya (8.3.5) gives the formula later adopted as India's national motto: 'satyam eva jayati nānṛtam' — 'Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood.' In this verse, truth 'established' (pratiṣṭhita) means truth has become the seeker's ground — not an occasional practice but a constitutional state. Such a person does not 'tell the truth' — they are truth. For them, Brahma-loka is not a distant reward but a present reality.

sk: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति ||
ro: teṣām · asau · virajaḥ · brahma-lokaḥ · na · yeṣu · jihmaṁ · anṛtaṁ · na · māyā · ca · iti ||
hi: उनका वह विरज (निष्कलंक, रज-रहित) ब्रह्मलोक है, जिनमें न जिह्म (कुटिलता) है, न अनृत (असत्य) है, और न माया (छल/कपट) है।
en: For them is that stainless (viraja) world of Brahman — for those in whom there is no crookedness (jihma), no falsehood (anṛta), and no deception (māyā).

ws.e: stainless — vi + rajas (impurity/passion); free from all taint; the Brahma-world is pure, untouched by the three guṇas
crookedness — jihma (crooked, oblique); dishonesty of conduct, indirectness, evasion
falsehood — an + ṛta (that which is not in accord with cosmic truth); lying, misrepresentation
deception / guile — māyā here means deliberate deceit/fraud (not the cosmic māyā of Advaita); trickery in dealings with others

gr: virajaḥ brahma-lokaḥ — 'the stainless Brahma-world': vi-rajas means 'free from rajas' — the cosmic impurity of passion, restlessness, and attachment. This world is pure in the ontological sense. Three disqualifiers: jihma (crookedness — moral obliquity), anṛta (falsehood — lying), māyā (deception — guile/fraud). The three form a descending series of dishonesty: crookedness → lying → active deception. The negative phrasing is significant: the Upanishad does not list virtues to acquire but vices to eliminate. The Brahma-world is already yours — you simply need to remove the disqualifications. This is the concluding verse of Question 1 — the answer is complete.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: prashna_upanishad_1.16 — This is the final verse of Question 1. The three disqualifiers — jihma, anṛta, māyā — form an ethical triad that complements the spiritual triad of tapas, brahmacarya, satya in the previous verse. The word 'māyā' here means deception/guile (interpersonal trickery), NOT the cosmic illusion of Advaita philosophy — that usage developed later. The Chāndogya (8.1.6) has a similar passage: 'na ha vā atrāpadāṁ jayaḥ / na jihmaṁ na māyā' — 'There (in the Brahma-city within the heart) is no place for sorrow; there is no crookedness, no deception.' The Muṇḍaka (3.1.8) echoes: 'nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā' — the Self is not attained by speech (which can be false) or by cleverness (which can be deceptive) but only by the one whom it chooses — and it chooses the truthful.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'विरज' = रजोगुण-रहित; ब्रह्मलोक = निर्गुण ब्रह्म-अनुभव। तीन दोष — जिह्म, अनृत, माया — ये मिथ्या-व्यवहार के तीन रूप हैं। जिसमें ये नहीं, वह सत्य में स्थित है — और सत्य = ब्रह्म।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'viraja' = free from rajas; Brahma-loka = the experience of nirguṇa Brahman. The three faults — jihma, anṛta, māyā — are three forms of false conduct. One who is free of these is established in truth — and truth = Brahman.
advaita.ins: The last word of the first question is about truth. Not metaphysics, not ritual, not theology — truth. Be straight, be honest, be transparent. That is the entry ticket to the stainless world.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'विरज ब्रह्मलोक' = भगवान् का शुद्ध, निर्दोष, दिव्य धाम। 'जिह्म-अनृत-माया-रहित' — भगवान् का धाम केवल शुद्ध हृदय वालों के लिए है; कपटी, झूठे और छली वहाँ नहीं पहुँच सकते।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'viraja Brahma-loka' = the Lord's pure, flawless, divine abode. 'Free from jihma, anṛta, māyā' — the Lord's abode is only for those with pure hearts; the crooked, the false, and the deceitful cannot reach it.
vishisht.ins: The Lord's door is open — but three guards stand at the threshold: Honesty, Truthfulness, and Transparency. If you cannot pass them, you cannot enter. No amount of ritual can bribe these guards.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'विरज' = राजसिक अशुद्धि से मुक्त; ब्रह्मलोक = शुद्ध चेतना का क्षेत्र। जिह्म, अनृत, माया — ये निम्न प्रकृति (lower nature) की विकृतियाँ हैं; इन्हें त्यागे बिना उच्च चेतना (higher consciousness) में प्रवेश नहीं।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo reads 'viraja' as free from rajasic impurity; Brahma-loka as the field of pure consciousness. Jihma, anṛta, māyā — these are distortions of the lower nature; without abandoning them, there is no entry into higher consciousness.
aurobindo.ins: Higher consciousness has its own immune system. Crookedness, falsehood, and deceit are pathogens that it automatically rejects. You cannot smuggle darkness into the light.

dp.q: 🔍 What are the three disqualifications — jihma, anṛta, māyā?
dp.a: The three vices listed as disqualifiers from Brahma-loka form a descending series of dishonesty: (1) Jihma (crookedness): the subtlest form — moral obliquity, indirectness, evasion. Not outright lying, but not being straight. Saying one thing and meaning another. Letting people draw false conclusions without technically lying. The crooked person is not a liar — he is worse: he is a manipulator. (2) Anṛta (falsehood): direct lying — saying what is not true. This is more obvious than jihma but still involves the intention to deceive. Anṛta is the opposite of ṛta (cosmic truth/order); to lie is to act against the grain of reality itself. (3) Māyā (deception/guile): active, deliberate fraud — constructing elaborate deceptions to mislead others. Note: 'māyā' here does NOT mean the cosmic illusion of Advaita philosophy (that technical usage developed later). Here it means interpersonal trickery — cheating, scheming, double-dealing. The three vices correspond to three levels of dishonesty: thought (jihma — crooked thinking), speech (anṛta — lying), and action (māyā — deceptive conduct). The Upanishad's message: total transparency is the prerequisite for the stainless world.

dp.q: 🔍 How does Question 1 answer 'Where do creatures come from?'
dp.a: Question 1 asked: 'kutaḥ imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante' — 'From where are creatures born?' Pippalāda's answer unfolds across 14 verses and is comprehensive: The ultimate source: Prajāpati, desiring offspring, performed tapas and produced a pair — Prāṇa (life-force/sun) and Rayi (matter/moon). All creatures arise from the interaction of these two principles (mantra 4). The cosmic mechanism: the sun (Prāṇa) energises all beings through its rays in all directions (mantras 5-8). The Vaiśvānara fire — universal, all-formed — is the visible manifestation of this Prāṇa (mantras 7-8). The two paths: creatures born from this process follow two paths after death — the pitṛyāṇa (path of Rayi, return) for those who rely on ritual alone, and the devayāna (path of Prāṇa, no return) for those who add knowledge (vidyā) to their practice (mantras 9-10). The practical applications: the Prāṇa-Rayi framework applies to the year (uttarāyaṇa/dakṣiṇāyana), the month (bright/dark fortnight), the day (day/night), and even to food and procreation (mantras 11-14). The ethical condition: the stainless Brahma-world is available only to those free from crookedness, falsehood, and deception (mantras 15-16). The answer is thus both cosmological (where creatures come from) and soteriological (where creatures can go).
